clue.text: They are not in, so the odds are against them

definitions.meaning: people left out of a group or circle, not admitted inside it
runners or contenders given little chance of winning by the bookmakers

explanation.surface: A group excluded from the in-crowd who are also unlikely to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: people excluded from a circle, and long-priced contenders in a race or contest.

clue.text: United Nations seizure taken ill

parts.note: a fit is a sudden seizure or attack

explanation.surface: A UN official falls sick after being grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taken ill is in poor health, not well enough for work or duty.

clue.text: Another time

definitions.meaning: a further one, as in 'a ... helping'
a unit of time, one sixtieth of a minute

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an additional one, and the base unit by which clocks measure time.

clue.text: Durban moved to Scotland?

indicators.note: the letters of the city name are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Imagining the South African city relocated to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging DURBAN gives a town on the East Lothian coast of Scotland, so the whole clue both builds and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coastal town east of Edinburgh, so it is literally a South African city's letters relocated to Scotland.

clue.text: Post off terms of reference

definitions.meaning: to send off money or documents by post
the scope of a body's authority or task

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to send payment; as a noun it is the brief or area of responsibility given to someone.

clue.text: Draughtsmen in security projects which can't be handled

definitions.meaning: artists working under cover, people who draw in secret
hidden sliding compartments in furniture that pull out but have no handles to grip

explanation.surface: Designers employed on classified schemes that are too sensitive to touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draughtsmen' are drawers, people who draw; 'projects' is the noun-turned-verb for things that jut out, as a drawer does when opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealed compartments in a desk or cabinet have no visible pull, and the phrase can also describe people who sketch covertly.

clue.text: Autodidactic aspirant?

parts.note: split 'auto' as car and 'didactic' as instructional: someone hoping to master a car while being taught

explanation.surface: Someone eager to teach themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Autodidactic' normally means self-taught, but here 'auto' is a motor car, so the aspirant is having lessons at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A person taking lessons to pass the road test is aspiring to qualify in a car.

clue.text: All added up its factors make it the ideal anaesthetic

definitions.text: All added up its factors make it

parts.note: ideal means flawless or perfect
an anaesthetic is something more numb-making: read 'number' as numb-er

explanation.surface: A drug that is the best choice for putting a patient under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' here is the comparative of numb: something that makes you more numb. The definition is the mathematical one: 6 = 1+2+3.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics, an integer whose proper divisors sum to itself, such as 6 or 28, has that special name.

clue.text: Diminutive big talker is of little calibre

parts.note: diminutive means small or tiny
a bore is a tedious person who talks too much

explanation.surface: A short windbag who is not much of a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calibre' suggests quality of character, but it is the bore width of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm with a narrow barrel, such as a .22 rifle, has a narrow calibre.

clue.text: Executed after being outstripped by those coming…

definitions.meaning: beheaded, having the head cut off
intercepted by people who got in front

explanation.surface: Someone put to death after being overtaken by pursuers.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots carry the reader on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means intercepted or diverted by someone getting ahead, and taken literally it means decapitated.

clue.text: To some degree a deserter of French revolutionary ideals

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A man who partly betrayed the ideals of the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat was a radical journalist of the 1789 revolution, killed in his bath by Charlotte Corday.

clue.text: Cut up trees short

indicators.note: the letters of the word are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Felling trees and chopping them into short lengths.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt, brief speech is clipped and abrupt.

clue.text: Deck fuss by the navy

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A commotion on board a warship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate or embellish it.

clue.text: … behind later

definitions.meaning: following in position, at the back of

explanation.walkthrough: The opening dots link back to the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works for following in place and following in time.

clue.text: Openly displayed like the sixth letter in the previous word

definitions.text: like the sixth letter in the previous word
definitions.meaning: the sixth letter of the alphabet is F; in the previous clue's answer, written downwards, F sits directly above T

explanation.surface: A remark about one letter being on show.
explanation.walkthrough: The previous word is the answer to 13 down, entered downwards in the grid; F, the alphabet's sixth letter, sits just above the T there.
explanation.definitionFit: Public, unconcealed actions are plainly visible; read in two parts, the word also describes a letter placed directly above T.

clue.text: Any integral number of units in the Roman calendar

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified whole number in mathematics
ones are units

explanation.surface: A puzzle about counting whole units in an ancient calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: N ones means any whole number of units. The definition is loose: the answer names a day within the Roman calendar, the ninth day before the Ides.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar each month had Kalends, Ides and this ninth-day-before-the-Ides marker.

clue.text: Don't punish the French gent!

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
a toff is an upper-class gentleman

explanation.surface: A plea to spare a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone from a penalty is to spare them; the imperative form matches 'Don't punish'.

clue.text: Ordinary seaman has to look after Belgian port

parts.note: to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: A junior sailor must care for things in a Belgian harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Sea ferry town in West Flanders, Belgium.

clue.text: Small wooden object around about 10

indicators.note: the number word goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: ten is 10
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A little carved item turning up at about ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned household items such as bowls and spoons made of timber are collectively called this.

clue.text: Miss Peep's anger has a simple solution

parts.note: Bo Peep is the nursery-rhyme shepherdess
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme girl's temper is easily resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' is a noun: an old word for a medicinal herb, which is what this blue-flowered plant is; 'solution' extends the picture of a herbal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is an old term for a medicinal herb, and this blue-flowered plant was used in folk remedies.

clue.text: Duel upset little Edward so was avoided

indicators.note: the letters of the word are upset and fall into a new order

parts.note: Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A duel unsettled young Edward, so he was given a wide berth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dodged or escaped from was evaded; the answer is a passive-sense past form here.

clue.text: Set-back after art centre gets levy

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed after the other piece

parts.note: the RA, the Royal Academy, is a London centre for art

indicators.note: the word is read back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setback at an arts venue leads to a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SET into TES. RA is the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Local property taxes in Britain were long charged under this name, a kind of levy.

clue.text: A renowned batsman is a handsome fellow

parts.note: Don Bradman, the great Australian cricketer

explanation.surface: A famous cricketer is a good-looking man.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Donald Bradman, 'the Don', is cricket's most famous batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Aphrodite loved a youth of great beauty, whose name now means any very good-looking young man.

clue.text: Bizarre eastern toxic compound

indicators.note: the word is compounded, its letters mixed into a new form

explanation.surface: A strange poisonous chemical from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a chemistry noun but signals TOXIC rearranged to XOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange or unusual things seem foreign and striking.

clue.text: Redesigned lower part of the spur

indicators.note: the word is redesigned with its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Lowering a redesigned component of a rider's spur.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiked revolving wheel at the end of a horseman's spur has this name.

clue.text: Following a dead king

parts.note: the late means the dead
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Coming after a monarch who has died.
explanation.definitionFit: Following in time means coming afterwards, subsequently.

clue.text: Richard, the acceptable face of Rock

definitions.meaning: the first name of the singer Sir ... Richard, reversed in the clue
a rock face is a steep sheer drop

explanation.surface: A clean-cut singer as the respectable side of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard was the wholesome early British rock 'n' roll star; a sheer rock face is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep rock face is a precipice, and the singer Cliff Richard was the clean-cut face of British rock.

clue.text: Indian striker in Morocco brawl

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: An Indian attacker caught up in a fight in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer or cricketer, but it is a snake that strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake of India that strikes at its prey.

clue.text: Desks for multiplication exercises

definitions.meaning: copying out times tables, as schoolchildren once did

explanation.definitionFit: Desks are furniture for penmanship; read otherwise, the phrase means writing out times tables.

clue.text: One piece of menswear or two pieces of women's winterwear

parts.note: a frock worn by a woman
an overgarment worn in winter

explanation.surface: Comparing a man's single garment with a woman's two.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal tailcoat worn by men for evening dress is one garment; split, it names a frock plus an overgarment.
